hints: A room is a connected component of floor cells using up, down, left, and right moves.
Scan every cell; when an unvisited floor cell is found, start a flood fill.
Mark cells when adding them to the search so each is processed once.
analogy: A room is a region you can walk through without crossing a wall.
example: The sample map has three separate groups of dot cells, so the answer is 3.
algorithm: Loop over all cells; for each unseen '.', run DFS/BFS over four-neighbor floor cells and increment the room count.
correctness: Flood fill visits exactly the cells connected to its starting cell; starting only at unvisited floor cells counts each component once.
complexity: O(nm) time and O(nm) space for an n-by-m map.
